questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Callous
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**caring'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Callous** means feeling or showing no sympathy for others.

 
 
• Example- He seemed **callous** when he delivered the horrible news.
 
 
 
• **Caring** means feeling or showing concern or kindness for others.
 
 
• Example- Mary is the most caring person you will ever meet.
 
 
 
• It is clear that '**callous**' and '**caring**' are opposite in meaning. Therefore the correct answer is '**caring**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cold** means lacking affection or warmth of feelings.
 
• **Insensitive** means showing or feeling no concern for others' feelings.
 
• **Hardened** means someone who has had so many bad experiences that nothing upsets or shocks them anymore.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

I __have completed__ the work two hours ago.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**completed**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **tense** in the sentence "I **have completed** the work two hours ago" is **present perfect tense.**
 
• **The present perfect tense** is used if the action **started in the past** but still has an **effect on the present**.
 
 
• **Example:** *I** have wanted** to go to the market since yesterday.*
 
 
 
• There is **no action** going on in the **present** according to the** given sentence** as the **work** has already been **completed** two hours ago. 
 
• This demands the usage of **simple past tense**.
 
 
• **Example:** *Mark **slept** like a baby yesterday. *
 
 
 
• Therefore, "completed" is the appropriate option as it is in the simple past tense. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Past tense** is divided into four types; **simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous.**
 
• **Simple Past tense** - denotes the completed action.
 
 
• **Example:*** I **ate **ice cream.*
 
 
 
• **Past Continuous tense** - denotes that the action was going on for some time but is over now.
 
 
• **Example:** *I **was eating** ice cream.*
 
 
 
• **Past Perfect tense** - denotes the action that has been completed sometime before the past.
 
 
• **Example:*** I **had eaten** ice cream before knowing it was unhealthy. *
 
 
 
• **Past Perfect Continuous tense **- denotes that the past action had continued sometime in the past.
 
 
• **Example:*** I **had been eating** ice cream before I caught cold. *

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**the**". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The article "**the**" is used to denote a **specific person or object**. 

 
 
• **Example:*** I want **the** book that you borrowed yesterday. *
 
 
 
• In the given blank, the **specific country** should be mentioned. 
 
• Moreover, **other options** denote **pluralism** whereas the **question** demands **singularity**. 
 
• Therefore, the appropriate answer is "the". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other **articles** include **"a" and "an".**
 
• "**A**" is singularly used in front of words whose **starting letter is not a vowel.**
 
 
• **Example**: *Ira wants **a pen.***
 
 
 
• "**An**" is singularly used in front of words whose **starting letter is a vowel.** 
 
 
• **Example:** *I ate **an** **apple** for a snack.* 
 
 
 
• **"Many, all and few"** are called **Determiners** which are used in plurals. 
 
• **Many** - denotes a lot of objects.
 
 
• **Example**: *Tim has **many** shoes.*
 
 
 
• **All **- denotes everything present.
 
 
• **Example:** *Ron wants **all** the coloured balloons.*
 
 
 
• **Few** - Denotes some of the objects.
 
 
• **Example**: *Mary lent me a **few** bucks.*

questions.question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Conferense**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **correct **spelling is "**Conference**".
 
• Here, the last "**c**" is making an "**s**" sound.
 
• If the **letter after "c"** is either "**e', "i", or "y"**, then it makes an "**s**" sound.
 
 
• **Example**: ***Ci**ty, **Ce**ntral, Boun**cy**.* 
 
 
 
• Therefore, "conferense" is the incorrect spelling of "conference". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**c**" does **not** have its **own sound**.
 
• It either makes a "**k**" sound or an "**s**" sound.
 
• If it comes **before "i, e, y"** it makes an "**s**" sound, otherwise, it makes a "**k**" sound. 
 
 
• **Example:** ***Cycl**e.*
 
 
 
• In "cycle", it initially makes "**s**" sound as it comes **before "y"** and then makes a "**k**" sound as it comes **before "l"**.
